headline: UN amb. Mike Waltz tells FT the US could be mired in an Iran stalemate a year from now
dek: Trump said the US could end the Iran war 'very quickly' but questioned whether to 'finish it off or just want to let it wither'; 'Iran is a failing nation, and we're taking all the oil out that we want'; said oil is getting out through Hormuz and 'we are getting everything we want'. Waltz told the…
sources: Donald Trump (South Lawn remarks + Florida rally, Friday); Mike Waltz to the Financial Times (Friday); Helima Croft, RBC Capital Markets (via lankaleader.lk)
fault_line: 'End it very quickly' vs 'a stalemate a year from now' — even Trump's own ambassador disagrees with the timeline.

sections.what_happened: Trump said the US could end the Iran war 'very quickly' but questioned whether to 'finish it off or just want to let it wither'; 'Iran is a failing nation, and we're taking all the oil out that we want'; said oil is getting out through Hormuz and 'we are getting everything we want'. Waltz told the FT the US could still be in a stalemate with Iran a year from now. Croft: oil rally reflects near-term escalation expectation; Brent $117.45 intraday / $116.72 settle, +10% in October.
sections.what_verified: Trump Friday remarks carried by wire family in prior scans (0700-02 Epic Fury); Waltz/FT via Tribune.pk + lankaleader.lk (T4 aggregators, FT interview is the primary); Croft/RBC via lankaleader.lk. Single-family retrieval this scan but quotes are primary-source statements.
sections.what_disputed: Waltz's own stalemate warning undercuts Trump's 'end it quickly' framing; markets pricing escalation (Brent $117) contradict 'getting everything we want'.
sections.why_matters: Trump's two clocks: 'finish it off' or 'let it wither' — while his UN ambassador warns of a year-long stalemate and oil traders price the escalation. Who's reading the war right?
sections.context: Background: UPDATE (big-missed; Friday Oct 23) -- Trump: 'We could end it very quickly... Iran is a failing nation, and we're taking all the oil out that we want'; asks 'do we want to finish it off or just want to let it wither?'; UN amb. Mike Waltz tells FT the US could be mired in an Iran stalemate a year from now; Helima Croft (RBC): 'Over soon' soundbites are no match for active missile fire

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump's two clocks: 'finish it off' or 'let it wither' — while his UN ambassador warns of a year-long stalemate and oil traders price the escalation. Who's reading the war right? The fault line our audience is arguing over: 'End it very quickly' vs 'a stalemate a year from now' — even Trump's own ambassador disagrees with the timeline.
